description: The plot illustrates how training loss and validation loss change over training steps for two experiments (Ex1 and Ex2) during an embedding and LM head training stage. The x-axis is labeled “Step,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 60,000 with regularly spaced tick labels every 10,000 steps. The y-axis is labeled “Loss,” is shown with scientific-notation tick labels (e.g., \(2\times10^0\), \(3\times10^0\), …, \(1.2\times10^1\)), and covers values from roughly just below \(2\times10^0\) up to about \(1.2\times10^1\). Four lines are shown: (1) “Ex1 Loss” is a solid blue line with circular markers, starting near 3.7 at step 0, dropping to about 2.05 by around 7,000 steps, and then flattening near 1.9 through the end (about 1.9 at 60,000 steps). (2) “Ex2 Loss” is a solid teal line with circular markers, starting near 3.1 at step 0, decreasing to about 2.9 by around 7,000–13,000 steps, then stepping down to roughly 2.2 near 19,000 steps and continuing gradually toward about 2.0 by 60,000 steps. (3) “Ex1 Validation Loss” is a dashed blue line with circular markers, beginning near 5.2 at step 0, falling to about 3.2 by around 7,000 steps, and then remaining close to ~3.1 with small decreases through 60,000 steps (ending around 3.1). (4) “Ex2 Validation Loss” is a dashed teal line with circular markers, starting near 11.1 at step 0, dropping sharply to about 4.6 by roughly the first few thousand steps, decreasing to about 4.4 by around 13,000 steps, then moving down toward ~3.3 by about 30,000 steps and staying near ~3.3 through 60,000 steps (ending around 3.3).
